blocks.html: Fan-out problem
blocks.text: Fan-out problem

blocks.html: A single produced message must be delivered to many consumers.
blocks.text: A single produced message must be delivered to many consumers.

blocks.html: The producer or broker ends up doing multiple copies and sends.

blocks.html: What goes wrong
blocks.text: What goes wrong

blocks.html: High load on producer/broker: one input becomes many outputs.
blocks.text: High load on producer/broker: one input becomes many outputs.

blocks.html: Network amplification: one message → N network sends.
blocks.text: Network amplification: one message → N network sends.

blocks.html: Uneven scaling: adding consumers increases work non-linearly.
blocks.text: Uneven scaling: adding consumers increases work non-linearly.

blocks.html: Latency spikes: slow consumers delay overall delivery if not isolated.
blocks.text: Latency spikes: slow consumers delay overall delivery if not isolated.

blocks.html: Why it is called “fan-out”
blocks.text: Why it is called “fan-out”

blocks.html: Visual reason
blocks.text: Visual reason

blocks.html: One input line splits into many output lines.
blocks.text: One input line splits into many output lines.

blocks.html: The shape looks like a hand fan opening outward.
blocks.text: The shape looks like a hand fan opening outward.

blocks.html: Technical meaning
blocks.text: Technical meaning

blocks.html: “Fan-out” means one-to-many distribution.
blocks.text: “Fan-out” means one-to-many distribution.

blocks.html: Opposite term: fan-in (many inputs → one consumer).
blocks.text: Opposite term: fan-in (many inputs → one consumer).

blocks.html: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Key takeaway

blocks.html: Fan-out is not inherently bad.
blocks.text: Fan-out is not inherently bad.

blocks.html: It becomes a problem when one message must be duplicated and delivered to many consumers without isolation or scaling control.
blocks.text: It becomes a problem when one message must be duplicated and delivered to many consumers without isolation or scaling control.

blocks.html: Fan-out problem = cost per message grows with number of consumers.
